thread.title: Apple Stock Nabs Price-Target Hike On Rising iPhone Prices | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Nabs Price-Target Hike On Rising iPhone Prices | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple stock received a price-target hike Wednesday on prospects for higher revenue and earnings due to rising average selling prices for the iPhone and Apple Watch.
X Bernstein analyst Toni Sacconaghi upped his price target on Apple ( AAPL ) to 225 from 200, but reiterated his market perform rating based on valuation. Apple stock fell 3.4% to close at 215.09 on the stock market today .
"We are raising our fiscal Q4 and fiscal 2019 revenue and EPS estimates, largely due to richer ASP (average selling price) assumptions for iPhone and Watch," Sacconaghi said in a note to clients.
He is predicting an iPhone average selling price of $800 in the fourth quarter vs. analyst estimates of $741. He is modeling earnings per share of $2.90 on sales of $63.3 billion. That compares with estimates for $2.77 in earnings per share and $61.3 billion in sales.

Apple Stock Needs iPhone Unit Sales Growth For fiscal 2019, Sacconaghi is predicting an iPhone average selling price of $813 vs. analyst predictions of $775. He is forecasting "flattish" iPhone unit sales growth in the current fiscal year.
He is modeling Apple to earn $14.15 a share on sales of $291.3 billion in fiscal 2019. That compares with Wall Street's prediction of $13.64 in earnings per share and $280.6 billion for the year.
However, Apple stock is unlikely to appreciate much if the company can't increase its iPhone unit sales, Sacconaghi said.
"We believe that iPhone unit growth is likely to be the critical metric for investors going forward," he said. "We see the stock likely continuing to outperform if iPhone units can grow in fiscal 2019, and the stock underperforming if units are down 3% or more."
CEO Calls For U.S. Data Privacy Regulations Speaking at a conference in Brussels on Wednesday, Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook called for a European-style federal data privacy law in the U.S.
Cook said modern technology has resulted in a "data industrial complex" where personal information is "weaponized against us with military efficiency," negatively impacting individuals and society as a whole, Engadget reported. Facebook ( FB ) and Twitter ( TWTR ) have been criticized for not doing enough to stop the abuse of their social media platforms.
Cook called the misuse of personal data by organizations a "crisis." He urged the rest of the world to follow Europe's lead with its recently enacted General Data Protection Rules.
He also used the opportunity to reiterate Apple's commitment to user data privacy .
Apple Planning Global Launch Of TV Service Apple's rumored streaming video service will launch in the first half of next year, according to a report Tuesday by the Information . The service will compete with Amazon ( AMZN ) Prime Video and Netflix ( NFLX ), it said.
Apple plans to launch the service first in the U.S. and make it available in more than 100 countries after a few months, the report said. It likely will offer original shows through its existing TV app. Apple also plans to offer access to third-party subscription video services through the app.
